headline_marked: Huawei Mate XT2: [[World's First Tri-Panel Foldable]] with Privacy Display
headline: Huawei Mate XT2: World's First Tri-Panel Foldable with Privacy Display
summary: The new Huawei Mate XT2 boasts a 10.2-inch expandable display and a built-in privacy screen, starting at $2,980.
details: Huawei has announced the Mate XT2, claiming the title for the world's first foldable smartphone with a built-in privacy display. This new device combines a tri-folding design with advanced privacy features, aiming to capture a significant share of the foldable market.

The Mate XT2 features a novel hinge mechanism that allows its displays to fold inwards. When folded, it presents a 6.5-inch display, which expands to a large 10.2-inch screen with a 3K resolution when fully opened. The phone runs on Huawei's in-house HarmonyOS.

Under the hood, the Mate XT2 is powered by Huawei's new Kirin 9050 Pro chip, offering a 42% performance boost over its predecessor. The camera system includes a 50-megapixel main sensor, a 40-megapixel ultra-wide, and a 50-megapixel periscope lens with 3.5x optical zoom. An 8-megapixel selfie camera is located on the interior display.

Pricing for the Huawei Mate XT2 starts at 19,999 yuan (approximately $2,980) for models with 16GB of memory. A variant with 1TB of storage and the privacy display feature is priced at 24,999 yuan (around $3,725). A collector's edition with 2TB of storage begins at 29,999 yuan (roughly $4,470).
Given Huawei's current status as a national security risk, the Mate XT2 is not expected to be released in the US market.

headline_marked: Apple's [[first foldable iPhone]] reportedly costs over $2,000
headline: Apple's first foldable iPhone reportedly costs over $2,000
summary: After years of anticipation, Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone this week, with early testers reporting positive experiences.
details: Apple is reportedly set to unveil its first foldable iPhone this week, entering the market over five years after Samsung's initial offering. This launch is highly anticipated, especially as Tim Cook hands off CEO duties to John Ternus.

Sources indicate the foldable iPhone will come with a price tag exceeding $2,000, positioning it as a premium device. Early testers have described the phone as having a premium feel, fitting comfortably in pockets, and unfolding into a large, iPad-like display.

The device is expected to feature a 5.5-inch cover display that expands to 7.8 inches when unfolded. To achieve a pocketable form factor when folded, Apple has reportedly made some compromises, including the omission of a telephoto camera, though it will retain a dual-lens main and ultra-wide rear camera system.

Rumors suggest the inclusion of MagSafe for charging and accessories, but a potential departure from Face ID in favor of a side-mounted Touch ID fingerprint sensor for space-saving. The foldable iPhone is also expected to support split-screen multitasking.

Addressing a common issue with foldable phones, Apple has reportedly developed a display that minimizes the visibility of the screen crease. The phone will run iOS, leveraging the power of Apple's latest chips.

Beyond the foldable device, Apple is also expected to announce updates to its AirPods, potentially including built-in cameras with 'Visual Intelligence' features, and refresh its HomePod smart speaker line.

New models in the iPhone 18 line are also anticipated, though leaks suggest the standard iPhone 18 might be released six months after the premium Pro and Pro Max models, a departure from Apple's usual release strategy.
